messages:
Anya: Heads-up: the py/ts SDK canary that adds the new route header is causing weird quota attribution in the console for a few tenants. Seen doubled counts for 'acme' :eyes:
Liam: ugh, what header did the canary send? can you paste the snippet?
Anya: sure — minimal patch we shipped in py: 
```python
headers = {
  'Authorization': f'Bearer {key}',
  'X-RI-Route-V2': json.dumps({'route_id': 'r-123', 'priority': 'low'})
}
```
Liam: thanks. TS version mirrors that with `X-RI-Route-V2` too.
Sara: console mapping still expects `X-RI-Route` (v1). our dashboard aggregation code does a naive header-first mapping so v2 is getting folded twice during backfill.
Matt: that explains the double-count. two things to consider: normalize on ingestion OR make SDK send both headers during a transition window.
Jordan: normalization on the router side is safer: accept both X-RI-Route and X-RI-Route-V2, map to canonical route id before metering. fallback should prefer V2 if present.
Anya: agree, but router changes need a short bake — can we patch SDK quickly to stop sending the legacy header duplication? maybe opt-in flag so we don't flip everyone.
Matt: propose feature-flag `sdk_routehdr_v2` default off. set canary tenants opt-in. rollout 2 phases: SDK opt-in -> router normalize -> flip default.
Liam: telemetry ask: add a field `route_hdr_version` to outgoing telemetry events so console can separate v1/v2 attribution. that will make debugging easier without changing meter logic.
Sara: +1. we should also tag the console tile to show route_hdr_version and a small sparkline for mismatch rate. UX ask from product.
ci-bot: deploy-bot: Canary monitor alert at 2026-03-22T15:55:23Z — canary group error rate +2.1%, quota burn +18%, latency +12% :warning:
Anya: rolling back the SDK canary now to stop more noise. I'll post the rollback PR link in a sec.
Jordan: create a short server-side normalization patch and smoke test on staging. I can take that today.
Matt: assigned follow-ups: 1) Anya — rollback and feature-flaged build (PR). 2) Jordan — router normalize patch + unit tests. 3) Liam/Sara — telemetry field + console tile mock. 4) Ops — watch canary signals for 24h.
Anya: PR: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/7421 — rollback commit + flag. rolling back now :shipit:
Sara: adding a small eval to catch double-attribution in our quality checks (prompt-level sampling) so we catch regressions in future.
Liam: once router normalize lands, let's run a small reconciler job to fix historical mis-attribution for affected tenants.
Anya: thanks all. we'll re-run the canary with the flag on and telemetry enabled before any default flip. :+1:
deploy-bot: Canary monitor resolved at 2026-03-22T16:05:10Z — metrics trending back to baseline.
